posts.s: We're investigating a potential issue with Microsoft Intune and checking for impact to your organization. We'll provide an update within 30 minutes.

This event is a continuation of the issue previously communicated via IT1547988. Our monitoring has identified an increase in delays affecting check-ins for Microsoft Intune-enrolled Windows devices. Our investigation indicates that an issue in a recent Windows update is causing initial device check-in attempts to fail, while subsequent automated and manual attempts remain unaffected. We're continuing to analyze the changes introduced in the recent Windows update to isolate the specific root cause and determine an appropriate remediation strategy.
We've confirmed that a component introduced in a recent Windows update is causing the issue and are developing a fix. We'll provide an estimated release timeline once one is available.

We’ve confirmed that a recent Windows security update, MSRC144654, can cause a single check in to fail during installation. We’re developing a fix to address this issue and anticipate its release for early December 2026. We’ll provide a better estimate for the delivery of our fix when available.

posts.s: We’re investigating an issue impacting multiple Microsoft 365 services and we've determined the affected infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors. We're restarting and repairing impacted portions of this infrastructure to restore capacity, and reviewing an unexpected increase in a specific type of service traffic to determine whether it's contributing to the elevated load. In parallel, we're evaluating options to redirect traffic to alternate infrastructure to expedite relief.

We've completed redistributing connection traffic across our worldwide infrastructure, and we're moving additional traffic off the affected infrastructure to further reduce load. We're also restarting affected servers to return them to service. In parallel, we're investigating whether the elevated traffic reflects a genuine increase in requests or a shift in how traffic is being routed across our infrastructure.

We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact. As a precaution, we've paused all deployments and configuration changes while we review recent changes for any correlation to this event. We've determined that the elevated load isn't driven by an overall increase in traffic, but by a large number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable, which is shifting load onto the remaining infrastructure. We're investigating what's causing these servers to become unavailable while we work to safely return them to service.

We've identified that affected servers are failing automated health checks, which is causing them to become unavailable, and this may be related to a recent change to a component involved in processing those checks. We're testing a configuration change on a subset of affected infrastructure to address this and, if successful, will apply it more broadly. In parallel, we've initiated a restart of all affected servers and are validating whether they're successfully returning to service. This quick update is designed to give the latest information on this issue. Next update by: Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 10:00 PM UTC

While we haven't identified any recent changes that correlate with the start of impact, our investigation indicates the failed health checks may originate from a specific component on the affected servers that's responsible for processing them. We're deploying a targeted change to bypass this component on a subset of servers to validate whether this restores availability, and we've taken steps to prevent additional servers from being removed from service while we work to return the affected servers to service. We're also investigating why affected servers are experiencing elevated processor usage while handling requests.

While validating the targeted change, we found that many of the affected servers have become unresponsive, which is preventing us from confirming whether the change is effective. We're restarting these servers so they can come back online with the change in place, and we're applying the same approach to additional affected portions of our infrastructure to validate the results more broadly. Next update by: Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 9:30 PM UTC This quick update is designed to give the latest information on this issue.

We've validated an alternative health check method on a subset of affected infrastructure, which allowed the servers in that subset to successfully return to service, and we're now applying this change more broadly. We're also preparing an automated recovery process to continually detect and restart unresponsive servers, to help keep them in service while this change progresses. Additionally, our review of recent changes has identified a small number of configuration updates that we're investigating as potential contributors to the issue.

We're continuing to work through restarting and validating the affected servers to safely return them to service, and we're exploring opportunities to expedite this process. In parallel, we're assessing whether reverting the small number of recent configuration updates we identified could help accelerate recovery. Next update by: Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 10:30 PM UTC This quick update is designed to give the latest information on this issue.

We’ve also shifted traffic and connections to alternative pathways wherever possible and have observed limited recovery in some regions. We've streamlined our recovery process to expedite returning the remaining affected servers to service. To further support recovery, we're implementing protective traffic management measures in a specific location to reduce load on the affected infrastructure, and we'll expand these measures to additional locations if we observe positive results. As capacity is restored, users may experience a gradual recovery as their clients reconnect to the service.

While the servers we've returned to service initially remain healthy, we've observed that they can become unresponsive again once they begin receiving traffic. We're analyzing diagnostic data from these servers with our networking and platform experts to determine what's triggering this behavior. Building on the protective traffic management measures we've implemented, we're also temporarily limiting which types of traffic can reach the affected infrastructure in specific locations. This will help us determine whether a particular type of request is contributing to the impact and allow us to restore service incrementally. We're preparing a configuration change to address this behavior that can be applied across all affected servers, and we're validating it on a subset of servers before applying it more broadly alongside restarts of the affected infrastructure. We're observing partial recovery across regions in which we've applied these adjustments; however, these actions aren't resulting in sustained recovery, so we're reviewing what additional actions we can take to improve overall infrastructure stability.

This occurs when the backend servers outbound service cannot properly route to the backend machines. We’re continuing to observe heightened volume due to traffic rebalancing actions that we have taken throughout this event. We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused you and your business. We know the trust you place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services. This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions. As infrastructure stabilizes, we're still draining queued messages and rebalancing traffic, so customers may see improved sign-in/access while delivery and processing continue to catch up. We do not have an ETA for full recovery yet. Service access can recover before mail flow fully normalizes.

We continue to observe sustained service recovery across the previously affected environments. Due to the severity of impact this incident caused, we're monitoring for an extended period to ensure no additional mitigative actions are required. In parallel, we're monitoring the backlog of email messages accrued during this event to ensure all process successfully before considering the issue resolved. We're addressing all impact scenarios for dependent and related Microsoft 365 products as listed in the "More info" section below, and believe the majority of those impacted scenarios have been addressed.

We’ve confirmed continued recovery across previously affected environments. We’ll maintain monitoring to ensure the mitigation actions taken remain effective and track processing of the email backlog accumulated during the event. We’re continuing to address any open impact scenarios across dependent and related Microsoft 365 products, as detailed in the ‘More info’ section below. We believe the majority of these scenarios have been addressed, with work continuing on any remaining scenarios.

This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions. Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration. We will provide a full post-incident report once our review is complete.
